chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you stand in the first two rak'ahs and do not perform the Tashahhud, and you remember before you bow, then sit and perform the Tashahhud; and if you do not remember until you have bowed, then continue in your prayer as you are. So when you have finished, perform two prostrations (Sajdatan) without bowing in them, then perform the Tashahhud that you missed.
ai.seo_question: What should I do if I forget the Tashahhud in the first two rak'ahs of my prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of *Sajdat al-Nasī'* (prostrations of forgetfulness) specifically for omitting the Tashahhud, distinguishing between early and late recall to determine whether the omission is rectified within the prayer or requires post-completion compensation. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on maintaining the structural integrity of the prayer while accommodating human error through specific remedial acts, ensuring the validity of the worship despite minor lapses in recitation.
